stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and null spec. Live preview across GO, UP, MX locales is a complex feature requiring both requirement elaboration (openspec first) and testability/security hardening (speckit second).

agentContributions.notes: Novel story — live preview capability does not exist yet. Attachment point is useContent (236 callers) and ContentstackContext, which all content components consume. Live preview plugs in there to propagate real-time updates. VCs derived from description since ACs are empty. All VCs are framed at our side of the Contentstack boundary (mocked client) per unreachable-service rule.

Openspec provided zero acceptance criteria, so all 13 ACs are new. I derived them from the story title '[GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS', openspec's architectural notes (useContent/ContentstackContext attachment point, mocked-client boundary), and standard edge-case/error/security/accessibility concerns. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/AC-2 cover both consumption paths (useContent hook and ContentstackContext) as openspec noted both. (2) AC-3/AC-4 cover disconnection/reconnection resilience. (3) AC-5 covers cold-start when preview is unavailable. (4) AC-6 prevents memory leaks from unmounted subscribers. (5) AC-7 ensures update isolation across content IDs. (6) AC-8 handles malformed payloads. (7) AC-9 addresses authentication/authorization. (8) AC-10 covers accessibility for dynamic content updates per WCAG live-region guidance. (9) AC-11 covers the preview-to-publish transition. (10) AC-12 ensures the feature is safely optional. (11) AC-13 addresses rapid-update debouncing. The original story description is extremely thin (just the title repeated), which limits precision — I recommend the product owner validate these ACs against their actual intent.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents contributed but in an imbalanced way. Openspec provided valuable architectural context (useContent hook with 236 callers, ContentstackContext attachment point, mocked-client boundary per unreachable-service rule) but failed to produce any acceptance criteria — a core deliverable. Speckit compensated by deriving all 13 ACs from the story title and openspec's architectural notes, covering consumption paths, reconnection resilience, cold-start, memory leaks, update isolation, malformed payloads, auth, accessibility, preview-to-publish transition, optionality, and debouncing. The ACs appear comprehensive and non-overlapping, but the source material was extremely thin (title only, no description). Speckit itself flagged that product owner validation is needed. The collaborative pipeline worked but the output precision is inherently limited without genuine requirements input. Human review required to confirm the 13 derived ACs match actual product intent before implementation proceeds.
